about.heading: One stack, two domains: electric vehicles and electric aircraft.
paragraphs: I am a senior in the University Honors Program at Santa Clara University, graduating in June 2027 with a double major in Electrical and Mechanical Engineering. I learn by building the whole stack, from schematic and firmware to CAD and fabrication.

On Bronco Racing, SCU's Formula SAE Electric team, I programmed the Orion BMS 2 for BR1, the team's first electric formula car, co-designed its shutdown and charging-shutdown circuits, architected the vehicle CAN bus, and hand-soldered a harness of 140+ thermistors whose placement improved thermal-measurement accuracy by about 50 percent. The high-voltage system was designed, built, programmed, and bench-validated. It was not energized at competition, a deliberate safety call. For BR2, the 2027 car, I am the Electrical System Officer and HV Engineer, working with the team across the electrical and tractive-system stack.

At STMicroelectronics I debugged a customer's 3-phase traction inverter on real hardware with Lauterbach JTAG, then independently diagnosed a DC-bus instability and implemented a parallel-capacitor fix, validated under load.

Raven is my flagship project: a tri-tiltrotor eVTOL built on the Flightory Stallion FPV airframe and redesigned in carbon-fiber composite. It is also the flagship aircraft of the stealth AI hardware startup I founded in 2026. FAA Part 107 is in progress.

experience.role: Electrical System Officer (ESO) & HV Engineer, BR2
bullets: Work with the team across the electrical and tractive-system stack for BR2 (the 2027 car), an all-new design with competition in June 2027.
BR2 accumulator design: 120s4p of Molicel P50B cells, 480 cells in all, about 432 V nominal and 504 V max.
Rules-first working model: every design decision traced to a cited FSAE rule.
Rebuilding the charging cart from scratch as the first BR2 hardware project (in progress).
Founded and lead, solo, a stealth AI hardware startup.
Raven, a tri-tiltrotor eVTOL, is its flagship aircraft.
Programmed, configured, and modified the Orion BMS 2 for BR1's 100s3p Molicel P45B accumulator (about 420 V max) and bench-validated it to the FSAE EV rules.
Hand-soldered a custom harness of 140+ thermistors; placement optimization improved thermal-measurement accuracy by about 50 percent, as measured.
Co-designed the shutdown and charging-shutdown circuits and caught protection-logic errors before fabrication.
Architected the vehicle CAN bus and wrote STM32 firmware for sensor interfacing, data logging, and diagnostics.
Installed and programmed the 540 V on-board charger and designed the charging cart with a deadman lock.

Outcome at FSAE 2026: the team completed the static events. The high-voltage system was designed, built, programmed, and bench-validated, and was not energized at competition, a deliberate safety call.
Joined Santa Clara University's Formula SAE Electric team as it built BR1, SCU's first electric formula car.
Supported Global Key Account customers in microcontroller project development across automotive and industrial applications.

Debugged a customer's 3-phase traction inverter on real hardware with Lauterbach JTAG and the StellarStudio IDE, resolving PWM timing faults, gate-driver issues, and current-sensing calibration errors.
Independently diagnosed a DC-bus instability and implemented a parallel-capacitor fix, validated under load with oscilloscope and logic analyzer.
Identified firmware bugs in motor-control algorithms (Clarke/Park transforms, space-vector modulation, PWM) and supplied corrected code.
Produced PWM and SVM parameterization guides for internal and customer-facing use.
Ran hardware teardowns of competitive automotive electronics modules and delivered Excel pivot-table analysis to ST marketing.
